sentences.text: Briefly noted the facts of the case are that the petitioners purchased the land in question through the registered sale deed in the year 1980.
The subject piece of land was subsequently converted from agricultural to non-agricultural purposes as per the provisions of Section 90-B of the Rajasthan Land Revenue Act, 1956.

The amount due was duly deposited with the respondents and thereafter,
the Pattas were also issued and the same were registered.
After issuance of the Patta, an FIR was registered by one Prema Ram under Sections 420, 468, 467, 471 & 120-B of IPC against the petitioners.
In the said FIR, a Negative Final Report was filed by the Police.
Thereafter, Prema Ram instituted a civil suit for permanent injunction.

While all these proceedings were undertaken by Shri Prema Ram, simultaneously, an application was also filed by him to the Municipal Council, Nagaur stating the facts mentioned above regarding filing of the FIR etc.
The Municipal Council, Nagaur, in its meeting held on 23.08.2012, cancelled the Pattas issued to the petitioners on the basis of alleged false Affidavits filed by the petitioners.
Aggrieved of the Resolution of Minutes of Meeting dated 23.08.2012 of the Municipal Council, Nagaur, the present writ petitions have been filed.

Learned counsel for the petitioners vehemently submitted that Pattas were rightly issued in favour of the petitioners and the Affidavits filed on their behalf were also correct and do not suffer from any infirmity.

He submits that the Pattas were issued after [2024:RJ-JD:2681] (3 of 4)
[CW-11223/2012] following due process of law and while issuing such Pattas, neither any provision of the Act nor any Rules was violated.

Learned counsel further submits that cancellation of the Pattas vide Resolution No. 3 (6) taken by the Municipal Council, Nagaur in its meeting dated 23.08.2012 was passed without giving any opportunity of hearing to the petitioners.

He submits that the action of the respondents is in gross violation of the principles of natural justice and the effect of passing the Resolution dated 23.8.2012 will have civil and evil consequences as the property which is legally vested in them will be taken away without following due process of law.

He, therefore,
prays that the writ petition may be allowed and the Minutes of Meeting dated 23.08.2012 to the extent of cancelling the Pattas issued to the petitioners may be quashed and set aside.

Learned counsel for the respondent-Municipal Council, Nagaur has not disputed the contentions raised by the counsel for the petitioners and he very fairly submits that the Resolution No. 3 (6) in the Meeting dated 23.08.2012 has been passed without giving any opportunity of hearing to the petitioners.
He submits that the Municipal Council, Nagaur may be permitted to take appropriate action in accordance with law to reach a just and fair decision in the matter.

Considering the submissions made at the Bar and taking note of the fact that a valid Patta was issued to the petitioners by the Municipal Council, Nagaur after following due process of law but in the Meeting held on 23.08.2012, the same has been cancelled without giving any opportunity of hearing to the petitioners, therefore, the action of the Municipal Council, Nagaur [2024:RJ-JD:2681] (4 of 4) [CW-11223/2012] cannot be held to be in consonance with the principles of natural justice as no opportunity of hearing was extended to the petitioners before cancelling the Pattas and, thus, in the opinion of this Court, the same is unsustainable in the eye of law.
In view of the discussions made above, the writ petitions merit acceptance and the same are allowed.
The Resolution No.3 (6) qua the petitioner passed by the Municipal Council, Nagaur in its Meeting Yashoda vs State Of Raj.

And Anr (2024:Rj-Jd:2681) on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138683510/
2 dated 23.08.2012 is quashed and set aside.
However, the respondent-Municipal Council, Nagaur will be free to take appropriate action in accordance with law, after giving a reasonable opportunity of hearing to the petitioners.
Stay petitions as well as other pending applications, if any, shall stand disposed of.

(VINIT KUMAR MATHUR),J 76-77-/VivekMishra/-
